issue.body:
Prior to this commit, i18n runtime logic relied on the assumption that provided translation is syntactically correct, specifically around ICU syntax. However provided translations might contain some errors that lead to parsing failure. Specifically when translation contains curly braces, runtime i18n logic tries to parse them as an ICU expression and fails. This commit validates ICU parsing result (making sure it was parsed correctly) and throws an error if parsing error happens. The error that is thrown also contains translated message text for easier debugging.

**Note**: the check and the error message introduced in this PR is a safeguard against the problem that led to unhandled i18n runtime logic crash. So the framework behavior remains the same, we just improve the error message and it should be safe to merge to the patch branch.

Resolves #35689.

body:
Hi @pacocom, thanks for reporting this issue. Adding extra text bindings in translations (like you described in your message) would not work in Ivy due to the fact that the i18n model has changed.

In View Engine translations were embedded into a template first and compilation happened after that for each locale (which was time and resource consuming). In Ivy the model is different and template compilation is performed first and translation happens after that. As a result in Ivy translations should not contain extra constructions like text bindings. The proposed solution is to refactor the logic in a template (may be split original i18n block into chunks, use ICU syntax or have an extra element with `*ngIf`) to avoid the need to add extra text bindings in translations.

The error that you mentioned in your message was caused by the fact that i18n runtime logic tried to parse the `{{ period }}` in translated message as an ICU and failed. I've just created a PR https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/35923 to verify whether ICU parsing was successful before ICU processing to provide more descriptive error message.

Thank you.
